correctness.rationale: Expand the two SDIRK stage resolvents as Y_j=y+O(h), giving scaling s_i=y_i/max(y_i,eps)+O(h) uniformly on the mass simplex. The exact corrected resolvent then has drift G phi_eps(y)+O(h); uniform Lipschitz stability and discrete Gronwall yield global O(h) shadow-flow convergence including nonnegative boundary data. For α>β, monotonicity of phi_eps and the strictly decreasing scalar drift yield one attracting equilibrium. Solving respectively both-below-floor, mixed and both-above-floor balances gives the square-root, quadratic and true-equilibrium branches with exact matching boundaries. At exact ydagger the stage predictors equal ydagger for every h; inversion gives delta=h{β z^2/max(z,eps)-α x^2/max(x,eps)}/{1+h[α x/max(x,eps)+β z/max(z,eps)]}, strictly positive iff eps>x, with exact α=4,β=1,m=1,eps=2,h=1 value x_new=1/3. Direct rational tests and 21 branch checks corroborate, but analytic stability establishes the infinite limit.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Nurkhametova et al. preprint defines the final-stage correction with a denominator floor and analyzes positivity, conservation and ε-dependent error; it does not in the read sections state the exact fixed-floor shadow ODE, three-branch equilibrium, or all-positive-h displacement at exact equilibrium. The complete 2022 Torlo–Öffner–Ranocha study of different modified Patankar methods treats equilibrium preservation and near-zero effects but not this final-only floor-correction formula. Qualitative fixed-floor bias may be inferred from original consistency analysis, but not these exact identities as stated.
residual_risks: The original paper has multiple versions: the accessible full HTML is the revised August 2026 version; claims refer specifically to the v1 equation numbering (25),(29), so equivalent revision details should be checked if altered.

value.rationale: A sharp method-design boundary shows unconditional positivity and conservation can coexist with systematic equilibrium bias under refinement. The three regimes quantify exactly when a minority component is biased, and the all-h explicit equilibrium displacement gives a useful well-balancing diagnostic for a natural two-state test problem.

final_claim: For the final-only fixed-epsilon Patankar SDIRK21 correction applied to a two-state reversible exchange generator alpha>beta>0, timestep refinement converges with O(h) error to xprime=beta phi_eps(m-x)-alpha phi_eps(x), phi_eps(u)=u^2/max(u,eps), not generally to the original linear ODE; the shadow equilibrium has exactly three explicit regimes, and the original equilibrium moves at every h>0 whenever eps exceeds its minority component.
